title: The Erdős–Mordell inequality for interior points of arbitrary triangles in taxicab geometry
statement:
Let $ABC$ be an arbitrary triangle in the taxicab plane, and let $P$ be an interior point of $ABC$. Denote by $R_A$, $R_B$, and $R_C$ the taxicab distances from $P$ to the vertices $A$, $B$, and $C$, respectively, and by $r_a$, $r_b$, and $r_c$ the corresponding taxicab distances from $P$ to the sides opposite $A$, $B$, and $C$.

**Erdős–Mordell open problem.** In taxicab geometry, the inequality

$$
R_A+R_B+R_C\geq\frac{3}{2}\left(r_a+r_b+r_c\right)_{\text{\micros \symbol{5}}}
$$

should hold for every interior point of every triangle $ABC$.

The preceding theorem establishes the inequality for an interior point of a triangle in an appropriate position; the open problem asks whether it holds for arbitrary triangles, reflecting the dependence of taxicab distance on the coordinate-system rotation.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.08758

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2019). “For an arbitrary triangle $ABC$ we set the following open problem (illustrated by Fig. 5).”
source_name: Maja Petrovic, Branko Malesevic and Bojan Banjac, “On the Erdos-Mordell Inequality for Triangles in Taxicab Geometry”, arXiv:1901.08758 (2019).
